findings.title: 7/29 onboard captures aim at the unusable 7/29 vanishing point; the 7/29 cards' guide and the header claim 'same aim as the evaluation camera' do not hold
findings.problem: capture_cg_vpfix.mjs solves pitch/yaw per session from vp_calib.json summary[race]. For fuji_aim_01 that is the 7/29 vanishing point (651.8, 186.7) from 11 wet frames with IQR 610-678 px in u and 176-198 px in v, which T3 summarize.py marks 'not usable (wet, 11 unstable frames)'; T3 analyze.py vp() uses only the 7/30 point (624.4, 196.8) for both days (same mount: the dashboard edge is at the same pixels). So the 7/29 clipping numbers printed on the cards (dt/dS at f711/h1.25) were computed with a camera pitched 12.88° / yawed +1.64°, while the 7/29 3DCG onboard images on the same cards are rendered at 13.72° / -0.48°. The row-276 guide on the 7/29 3DCG images therefore sits at ~10.0 m ahead instead of ~11.2 m (f 711, h 1.25, flat road), a ~1.2-1.3 m (~0.05 s at 90 km/h) along-track bias and a ~27 px (2.2°) horizontal shift on all 26 7/29 cards, comparable to the per-event values shown (typical 1.4 m). The header sentence '7/29は下向き13.7°・左向き0.5°…（評価資料でクリッピングポイントを測ったカメラと同じ向き）' is false for 7/29, and the 数字の読み方 statement that the guide is comparable relies on it.
findings.evidence: artifacts/event-comparison-2026-10-22/scripts/capture_cg_vpfix.mjs profileFor(race) -> VP[race]; cg/manifest_onboard_vpfix.json sessions.fuji_aim_01.profile pitchDeg 13.7179 yawDeg -0.4838 vs fuji_aim_2020_07_30 12.8807 / 1.6383; T3 vp_calib.json summary.fuji_aim_01 (frames 11, u_vp_iqr 610-678, v_vp_iqr 176-198); T3 analyze.py lines 40-49 (vp() reads fuji_aim_2020_07_30 only); T3 summarize.py line 389; build_page.py line 74 asserts the per-session aim; page header text. Reviewer arithmetic: 1.25/((276-196.8)/711) = 11.2 m vs 1.25/((276-186.7)/711) = 10.0 m; atan((651.8-624.4)/711) = 2.2°.
findings.fix: In capture_cg_vpfix.mjs add a --vp-session option (default fuji_aim_2020_07_30) so profileFor() solves both sessions from the 7/30 vanishing point, record vanishingPointSession in the manifest, and recapture all 106 onboard images (about 50 s on the running 5200 server) into cg/ with manifest_onboard_vpfix.json (keep the previous run under cg/superseded/). In build_page.py assert both session profiles equal the 7/30 solution (pitch 12.8807, yaw 1.6383) and replace the header sentence with: '下向きと左右の向きは、車の真正面が7/30の動画の消失点に来るように合わせました（下向き12.9°・右向き1.6°。7/29の消失点は雨で11コマしか測れず不安定なので、評価資料と同じく両日とも7/30の値を使っています。カメラの取付は両日同じです）'. Rebuild and re-run qa_page.mjs. Optional: re-run adversarial_compare.py for the 26 7/29 events (the homography is then the identity for 7/29 too) and record the 7/29 counts in verify.json round1Recheck.
findings.acceptance: cg/manifest_onboard_vpfix.json sessions.fuji_aim_01.profile.pitchDeg == 12.8807 and yawDeg == 1.6383 (equal to fuji_aim_2020_07_30) with a manifest field naming the vanishing-point session; summary failures 0, onboardActive 106; every *_cg_onboard.jpg mtime inside the new run window; build_page.py asserts the common aim; the page no longer prints '下向き13.7°・左向き0.5°' and states that both days use the 7/30 vanishing point; qa_page.mjs passes (0 failures, 531 images, 110 guides).

findings.title: k1 L5 has two vibration bursts; the '5 of 6 laps late' count relies on the first (medium-confidence) burst without saying so
findings.problem: On 7/30 L5 the logger shows two primary bursts at k1: 33.061 s (RR only, confidence medium, audio-confirmed, dt +0.204 s) and 33.670 s (VA+RR, confidence high, not video-confirmed, flag onsetBoundedByPreviousContact, dt -0.405 s). The 3DCG contact (33.265-33.491 s) lies between them. B counts L5 among the five late laps using the first burst; with the second burst the 3DCG would be 0.41 s early. Both bursts are plotted in the chart (n 20 includes both), which a careful reader will notice.
findings.evidence: event_table.json kerbContacts fuji_aim_2020_07_30 lap 5 k1 (two entries, both primary); kerbPasses L5 k1 truthConfidences ['medium','high']; summary.worst.contactFirstBlock_events (L5 k1 dS +13.88 / dt -0.405).

overallAssessment: All eleven round-1 findings were implemented and verified against their acceptance checks; three of my own round-1 clauses were wrong and the implementers were right to reject them (k1 '約0.15秒' under the 50 % rule, 'the nose never turns before the steering', the yaw formula sign, and 'below the line' for L1-k9). The analysis is internally consistent: verify_join allOk on re-run; event_table k1, tolerance, turn-in and camera-scale numbers reproduce; and a new cross-check shows the working-tree captures used for the comparison page match the origin/master T4 pose traces within 0.2 mm and 0.001 deg at all 106 event instants, so the page images and the report numbers describe the same drawn car. Both HTML pages render with 0 errors and 0 page overflow at 390/1100 px in light and dark. The one issue that still misleads is on the comparison page: the 7/29 onboard images were aimed at the 7/29 vanishing point that T3 rejected as unusable, so the 26 7/29 cards show a 3DCG camera pitched 0.84 deg lower and yawed 2.2 deg differently from the camera behind their printed clipping numbers (row-276 guide ~1.2 m nearer), and the header's 'same aim as the evaluation camera' is false for that day; recapturing with the 7/30 point (as T3 did) is a one-step fix. Remaining items are low-severity polish (phone-width tables, the k1 L5 double burst, the time-sign note in the camera table, a stale sentence in verify.json). For the orchestrator: WORKLOG entries 12:44 ('k1 約0.15秒') and 20:43 ('yaw stayed at the 10/03 estimate', 'image check confirmed the correction direction') are now contradicted by the stored outputs and should be reworded when the loop is recorded.
